santos-passos.name: Church of Our Lady of Consolation and the Holy Steps
santos-passos.short: André Soares' Baroque church, with 19th-century twin towers and a Via Sacra, on Largo da República do Brasil
santos-passos.long: It all began with a chapel to Our Lady of Consolation, founded in March 1576 on the Campo da Feira. In 1769 the brotherhood commissioned a new church from the architect André Soares (1720–1769) — probably his last work: he died before designing the interior. The church was finished in October 1785. Two towers on the façade, the staircase and the balustrade were added in the 19th century. Inside are a Rococo altarpiece and tribune by the carver José António da Cunha. Beside the church stand the “Passos”, small Via Sacra chapels with painted wooden figures of the Passion.
santos-passos.history:
The church began as a small chapel dedicated to Our Lady of Consolation. The brotherhood of Nossa Senhora da Consolação had it built in March 1576 on the Campo da Feira, the fairground north-west of the historic centre — the site of today's Largo da República do Brasil.

In 1769 the same brotherhood commissioned a much larger church from the architect André Soares (1720–1769), one of the leading masters of the Baroque in Braga and Guimarães. It was probably his last work: he died that same year, before designing the interior. As planned, the church has a longitudinal, single-nave layout with concave angles and a chancel; the façade was given a curved form and the towers a dynamic silhouette. Construction was completed in October 1785.

In the 19th century the church was completed: two towers rose on the main façade, and a stone staircase, balustrade and sculptures were added, producing a strong scenographic effect; the Casa do Despacho was built at the same time. Inside, the carved altarpiece and tribune by the master carver José António da Cunha survive, adorned with gilded Rococo carving. Later the brotherhood of São Gualter moved here, and a 19th-century image of the saint was made.

A distinctive part of the ensemble is the Oratórios, or Passos — small chapels that form a Via Sacra. Inside them are painted wooden figures representing the stages of Christ's Passion; this is where the church's second name, “of the Holy Steps”, comes from. The church stands on the axis of Largo da República do Brasil, beside its garden and the road leading to the Penha cable car.

In 1993 the church and oratories were listed as an Imóvel de Interesse Público (Decree no. 45/93, Diário da República, 30 November 1993).

The nave ends in the chancel, and the concave angles of its walls give the interior the movement of late Baroque. Although the interior was designed after Soares' death, it follows his intention, and the church is counted among the most expressive works of Baroque space in Guimarães. The brotherhood of Our Lady of Consolation and the Holy Steps, which commissioned the church, held services and processions here for centuries; in the mid-19th century the brotherhood of São Gualter, one of the city's most venerated saints, joined it. The Oratórios — the “Passos” — stood in different parishes as Stations of the Cross, and their wooden figures were carried out during Holy Week. Today the church is still a working parish church and the chief landmark of the Campo da Feira — the old fairground that was the city's gateway on the Penha side; in the 19th century a square with a garden, staircases and balustrades took shape here, and the church's twin towers became visible from the approaches to the city. Every August the church becomes one of the centres of the Gualterianas festivities, and its staircase and square serve as a stage for the townspeople. Its twin towers and balustrade give the silhouette a solemnity typical of Portuguese Baroque. More than two centuries on, it remains a landmark on the Campo da Feira.

santos-passos.tip: Entry is free outside service times. The church stands on Largo da República do Brasil, in front of a neat garden, and from here it is easy to walk on to the lower station of the Penha cable car. Combine it with a walk through the Campo da Feira and the historic centre. Processions are held here in Holy Week, and the square's setting is one of the finest in the city.
